cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Supraspinatus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Initiates the first ~15° of arm abduction and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Supraspinous fossa of scapula and overlying fascia.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior facet of greater tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Infraspinatus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates the arm and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Infraspinous fossa of scapula and overlying fascia.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Middle facet of greater tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Teres major

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; assists extension of the arm from a flexed position.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lower subscapular nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior surface of inferior angle and adjacent lateral border of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial lip of intertubercular sulcus of humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Teres minor

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates the arm; weakly adducts the arm; stabilises the humeral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Axillary nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Middle part of lateral border of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Inferior facet of greater tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Latissimus dorsi

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm; can help raise the trunk toward the arms during climbing.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Spinous processes T7–T12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest and lower ribs; variable slip from inferior angle of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Floor of intertubercular sulcus of humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Subscapularis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Medially rotates and adducts the arm; stabilises the humeral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Subscapular fossa of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser tubercle of humerus and shoulder joint capsule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deltoid

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Middle fibres abduct the arm; anterior fibres flex and medially rotate; posterior fibres extend and laterally rotate.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Axillary nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral third of clavicle, acromion and spine of scapula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Deltoid tuberosity of humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pectoralis major

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; clavicular head flexes the arm; sternocostal head extends a flexed arm.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral and medial pectoral nerves (C5–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial half of clavicle; sternum; upper six costal cartilages; aponeurosis of external oblique.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral lip of intertubercular sulcus of humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Biceps brachii

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow; assists shoulder flexion; long head helps stabilise humeral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle of scapula. Short head: tip of coracoid process.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Radial tuberosity and forearm fascia via bicipital aponeurosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Brachialis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Primary flexor of the elbow in all forearm positions.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6); lateral part often receives a small radial nerve contribution.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Distal half of anterior humerus and adjacent intermuscular septa.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Coronoid process and tuberosity of ulna.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Triceps brachii

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the elbow; long head also extends and adducts the arm and helps resist inferior displacement of the humeral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Radial nerve (C6–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle. Lateral head: posterior humerus superior to radial groove. Medial head: posterior humerus inferior to radial groove.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Olecranon of ulna and forearm fascia.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pronator teres

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Pronates the forearm and weakly flexes the elbow.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Median nerve (C6–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Humeral head: medial epicondyle. Ulnar head: coronoid process.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral surface of mid-radius.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor carpi radialis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Median nerve (C6–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common flexor tendon from medial epicondyle of humerus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of second metacarpal, often with slip to third metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palmaris longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Weakly flexes the wrist and tenses the palmar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Median nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common flexor tendon from medial epicondyle of humerus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor carpi ulnaris

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve (C7–T1, mainly C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Humeral head: medial epicondyle. Ulnar head: olecranon and posterior border of ulna.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Pisiform, hook of hamate and base of fifth metacarpal via pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor carpi ulnaris

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends and adducts (ulnar deviates) the wrist.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle via common extensor tendon and posterior border of ulna.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of fifth metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends digits 2–5, chiefly at MCP joints and via extensor expansions at IP joints; assists wrist extension.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle via common extensor tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Extensor expansions of digits 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor carpi radialis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends and abducts the wrist; helps stabilise the wrist during gripping.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of radial nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle via common extensor tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of third metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor carpi radialis longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends and abducts the wrist; helps return a flexed wrist toward neutral.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Radial nerve (C6–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of second metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Brachioradialis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the elbow most effectively with the forearm in mid-pronation; helps return forearm toward neutral from pronation or supination.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Radial nerve (C5–C7, mainly C6).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Proximal two-thirds of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral distal radius just proximal to styloid process.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tendon of extensor pollicis longus

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Distal tendon of extensor pollicis longus muscle.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through the third extensor compartment, turns around Lister’s tubercle, then crosses the dorsum of the wrist to the thumb.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of distal phalanx of thumb.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits extensor pollicis longus force to extend the thumb, especially at the interphalangeal joint.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the medial border of the anatomical snuffbox.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor pollicis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the thumb at the MCP joint and assists extension at the carpometacarpal joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior radius and adjacent interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of proximal phalanx of thumb.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor pollicis longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; assists radial deviation of wrist.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior ulna, radius and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of first metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum superficialis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes PIP joints of digits 2–5; also flexes MCP joints and wrist.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Median nerve (C7–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Humero-ulnar head: medial epicondyle, ulnar collateral ligament and coronoid process. Radial head: superior anterior radius.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Sides of middle phalanges of digits 2–5 after each tendon splits around FDP tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Supinator

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Supinates the forearm, especially during unresisted or slow supination.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of radial nerve (C6–C7).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle, radial collateral and annular ligaments, supinator crest and fossa of ulna.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of proximal third of radius.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palmar (volar) carpal ligament / Guyon’s tunnel

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Palmar carpal ligament spans the anterior wrist superficial to flexor tendons, blending medially with structures around pisiform and hook of hamate.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Guyon’s canal lies superficial to the flexor retinaculum between pisiform and hook of hamate.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve and ulnar artery pass through Guyon’s canal.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: The palmar carpal ligament helps retain superficial flexor structures; Guyon’s canal provides a passage for the ulnar neurovascular bundle.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve compression in Guyon’s canal causes ulnar-sided hand sensory and/or intrinsic motor deficits depending on lesion level.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor retinaculum

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends obliquely across the dorsal wrist from distal radius to ulnar-sided carpal and forearm fascia.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Prevents bowstringing of extensor tendons at the wrist.

cards.question: Compartments
cards.answer: Forms six osteofibrous extensor compartments containing the wrist and finger extensor tendons.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies superficial to the extensor tendon compartments on the dorsum of the wrist.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Tendon-compartment inflammation beneath it includes conditions such as de Quervain tenosynovitis in the first compartment.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor pollicis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the thumb at the MCP joint and assists opposition.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial head: recurrent branch of median nerve (C8–T1). Deep head is often supplied by deep branch of ulnar nerve.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Flexor retinaculum and trapezium; deep head may arise from trapezoid/capitate region.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral base of proximal phalanx of thumb via lateral sesamoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor pollicis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts the thumb perpendicular to the palm and assists opposition.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent branch of median nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Scaphoid tubercle, trapezium and flexor retinaculum.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral base of proximal phalanx of thumb and extensor expansion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Adductor pollicis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts the thumb and is important for power grip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Oblique head: bases of 2nd/3rd metacarpals and capitate. Transverse head: shaft of 3rd metacarpal.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of thumb via medial sesamoid and extensor expansion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Opponens pollicis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Opposes the thumb by flexing and medially rotating the first metacarpal at the carpometacarpal joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent branch of median nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of trapezium.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral side of first metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Opponens digiti minimi

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Draws the fifth metacarpal anteriorly and rotates it to assist opposition/cupping of the palm.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial border of fifth metacarpal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digiti minimi

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the fifth digit at the MCP joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of fifth digit.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor digiti minimi

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts the fifth digit and assists MCP flexion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Pisiform and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of fifth digit and extensor expansion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lumbrical

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flex MCP joints and extend IP joints of digits 2–5.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lumbricals 1–2: median nerve. Lumbricals 3–4: deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral sides of extensor expansions of digits 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal interosseus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abduct digits 2–4 from the axial line through the middle finger; assist MCP flexion and IP extension.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of metacarpals.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Bases of proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of digits 2–4.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor retinaculum

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Laterally to scaphoid tubercle and trapezium; medially to pisiform and hook of hamate.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the roof of the carpal tunnel and prevents bowstringing of flexor tendons.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Median nerve and nine long flexor tendons pass deep to it in the carpal tunnel; ulnar nerve and artery pass superficial to it in Guyon’s canal.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Compression of the median nerve beneath it produces carpal tunnel syndrome.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Annular ligament (A1 pulley) and fibrous digital sheath

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Fibrous digital sheath attaches along the margins of phalanges and palmar plates; A1 pulley lies over the MCP joint.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Holds flexor tendons close to the phalanges, preventing bowstringing during finger flexion.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus tendons run within the digital synovial/fibrous sheath.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Thickening at the A1 pulley can cause trigger finger.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cruciform ligaments

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Flexible cruciate components of the fibrous digital sheath between annular pulleys.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Permit sheath deformation during finger flexion while helping retain flexor tendons close to the phalanges.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Alternate with annular pulleys in the fibrous flexor sheath of digits.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Annular ligament (A3 pulley)

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attaches around the palmar aspect of the PIP joint/volar plate region.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Maintains flexor tendons close to the digit and limits bowstringing.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Part of the fibrous digital sheath, between cruciform pulley segments.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Pulley injury can alter flexor tendon mechanics; A2 and A4 are particularly important for preventing bowstringing.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tendon of flexor pollicis longus

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Distal tendon of flexor pollicis longus muscle.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through the carpal tunnel, then through the flexor sheath of the thumb.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Palmar base of distal phalanx of thumb.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits force to flex the thumb, especially at the interphalangeal joint.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Runs between the sesamoids at the MCP region and within its own digital synovial sheath.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Four distal tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Pass through the carpal tunnel and digital sheaths; each splits into two slips around the FDP tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Sides of middle phalanges of digits 2–5.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmit force to flex the PIP joints.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: At the proximal phalanx each tendon splits at Camper’s chiasm to allow the FDP tendon to pass through.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Four distal tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Pass through the carpal tunnel deep to FDS tendons and continue through the split FDS tendons within the digital sheaths.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Palmar bases of distal phalanges of digits 2–5.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmit force to flex the DIP joints; also assist flexion at more proximal joints.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Give origin to the lumbricals in the palm.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Chiasma tendinum of flexor digitorum superficialis tendon

cards.question: Definition
cards.answer: The split in each FDS tendon through which the FDP tendon passes, also called Camper’s chiasm.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Allows FDS to insert on the middle phalanx while FDP continues distally to the distal phalanx.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Occurs along the proximal phalanx within the fibrous digital sheath.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Axillary artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of subclavian artery at lateral border of first rib.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through axilla and becomes brachial artery at inferior border of teres major; divided into three parts by pectoralis minor.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Superior thoracic; thoraco-acromial and lateral thoracic; subscapular, anterior circumflex humeral and posterior circumflex humeral.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Axilla, shoulder region, lateral thoracic wall and upper limb.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Cords of brachial plexus are named by their relationship to the second part of the axillary artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Subscapular artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Third part of axillary artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends along lateral border of scapula.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior axillary wall, scapular region and latissimus dorsi.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Largest branch of axillary artery; participates in scapular anastomoses through circumflex scapular branch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Circumflex scapular artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Subscapular artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through triangular space to posterior scapular surface.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Muscular and anastomotic branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Muscles and tissues around posterior scapula.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anastomoses with suprascapular and dorsal scapular arteries around scapula.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior circumflex humeral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Third part of axillary artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through quadrangular space with axillary nerve and winds around surgical neck of humerus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Deltoid, shoulder joint and muscular branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Deltoid, teres minor, shoulder joint and proximal humerus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Closely associated with axillary nerve at surgical neck of humerus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Brachial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of axillary artery at inferior border of teres major.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends medial arm, enters cubital fossa and usually divides opposite neck of radius into radial and ulnar arteries.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Profunda brachii, superior and inferior ulnar collateral, muscular and nutrient branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Main arterial supply to arm and source of forearm arteries.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Median nerve crosses from lateral to medial side; brachial pulse and blood pressure are assessed near cubital fossa.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Profunda brachii artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually proximal brachial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Accompanies radial nerve in radial groove around posterior humerus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Radial collateral and middle collateral arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior compartment of arm and elbow region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: At risk with midshaft humeral fractures along with radial nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deltoid branch

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually a branch of the thoraco-acromial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs in deltopectoral groove with cephalic vein.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Deltoid and adjacent pectoral region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Accompanies cephalic vein in deltopectoral groove.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial (middle) collateral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Profunda brachii artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends posteriorly toward elbow, usually with radial nerve branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior elbow region and triceps; contributes to periarticular elbow anastomosis.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anastomoses with recurrent interosseous artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radial collateral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of profunda brachii artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends toward lateral epicondyle, often accompanying radial nerve anterior to lateral epicondyle.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral elbow and adjacent muscles.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anastomoses with radial recurrent artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior ulnar collateral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Brachial artery in mid-arm.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends with ulnar nerve posterior to medial epicondyle.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial elbow region and adjacent muscles.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anastomoses with posterior ulnar recurrent artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of brachial artery in cubital fossa.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends lateral forearm beneath brachioradialis, becomes superficial distally, crosses anatomical snuffbox and enters palm between first dorsal interosseous heads.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Radial recurrent, palmar and dorsal carpal branches, superficial palmar branch, princeps pollicis and radialis indicis after entering hand.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral forearm, wrist and hand; major contributor to deep palmar arch.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Pulse palpable lateral to flexor carpi radialis tendon at wrist; artery crosses floor of anatomical snuffbox.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial branch of radial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Radial artery near distal forearm/wrist.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes into palm, usually through or over thenar musculature.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Thenar region and superficial palm.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Typically joins superficial palmar arch formed mainly by ulnar artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal carpal arch

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Anastomosis of dorsal carpal branches of radial and ulnar arteries, with interosseous contributions.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs across dorsal carpus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives dorsal metacarpal arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Dorsum of hand and digits through dorsal metacarpal/digital branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies deep to extensor tendons on dorsum of wrist.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: 1st dorsal metacarpal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually radial artery or dorsal carpal network.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs dorsally in first intermetacarpal region.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of thumb and index region on dorsum.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located near first dorsal interosseous muscle and anatomical snuffbox region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulnar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of brachial artery in cubital fossa.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes deep to pronator teres, descends medial forearm and enters hand superficial to flexor retinaculum through Guyon’s canal.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Anterior and posterior ulnar recurrent, common interosseous, muscular, palmar and dorsal carpal branches; continues mainly into superficial palmar arch.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial forearm and major superficial arterial supply of hand.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Travels with ulnar nerve in distal forearm, artery generally lateral to nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common interosseus artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Short proximal branch of ulnar artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes toward proximal interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Deep structures of forearm through terminal branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Very short arterial trunk near proximal radius/ulna.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior interosseus artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common interosseous artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes posteriorly through proximal interosseous membrane region to posterior forearm.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Recurrent interosseous and muscular branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior forearm extensor compartment.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Accompanies posterior interosseous nerve in posterior forearm.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior interosseus artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common interosseous artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends on anterior interosseous membrane with anterior interosseous nerve.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Muscular, nutrient and perforating branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Deep flexor compartment, radius/ulna and wrist.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies on anterior surface of interosseous membrane between deep forearm flexors.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial palmar arch

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Mainly terminal ulnar artery, usually completed laterally by superficial palmar branch of radial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Curves across palm deep to palmar aponeurosis and superficial to long flexor tendons.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Common palmar digital arteries and a proper digital branch to ulnar side of little finger.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Major blood supply to palm and digits.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: More superficial than deep palmar arch; level roughly corresponds to distal border of fully extended thumb.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palmar digital artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually common palmar digital arteries from superficial palmar arch.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Run toward interdigital web spaces.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Divide into proper palmar digital arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of fingers.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Travel with digital nerves in the sides of digits.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Proper palmar digital artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common palmar digital artery or direct branch of superficial palmar arch.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs along side of a finger.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Skin, subcutaneous tissues, tendon sheaths and phalanges of corresponding side of digit.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Accompanies proper digital nerve along lateral or medial aspect of digit.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal digital artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually dorsal metacarpal arteries from dorsal carpal network.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs along dorsal aspects/sides of digits.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Dorsal surfaces of proximal digits; distal dorsal digits also receive palmar digital contributions.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms dorsal vascular networks with palmar digital branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Brachial plexus

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Anterior rami of C5–T1, with possible prefixed/postfixed variation.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Roots pass between anterior and middle scalene muscles; trunks cross posterior triangle; divisions form behind clavicle; cords surround axillary artery in axilla.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Provides motor innervation to almost all muscles of te upper limb through its terminal and collateral branches.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Provides most cutaneous and joint sensation of the upper limb through its terminal branches.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Deficits depend on level: upper trunk injury classically affects C5–C6 functions; lower trunk injury affects C8–T1 functions; cord/terminal branch lesions produce more peripheral patterns.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Axillary nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C5–C6 from posterior cord of brachial plexus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through quadrangular space with posterior circumflex humeral artery, then winds around surgical neck of humerus deep to deltoid.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Deltoid and teres minor.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Skin over superolateral arm via superior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm; articular branch to shoulder.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Weak arm abduction beyond ~15°, deltoid wasting and numbness over regimental-badge area; vulnerable in surgical-neck fractures and anterior shoulder dislocation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C8–T1 from medial cord of brachial plexus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends medial arm, often accompanying basilic vein, then divides into anterior and posterior branches in forearm.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; cutaneous nerve.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Skin of medial forearm.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Isolated injury causes sensory loss or neuropathic symptoms over medial forearm without motor weakness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Musculocutaneous nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C5–C7 from lateral cord.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Pierces coracobrachialis, runs between biceps and brachialis, then continues as lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Coracobrachialis, biceps brachii and most of brachialis; elbow flexion and forearm supination via these muscles.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Lateral forearm via lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Weak elbow flexion and supination, reduced biceps reflex and sensory loss over lateral forearm.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Median nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C6–T1, often with C5 contribution; formed by lateral and medial roots from lateral and medial cords.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends with brachial artery, crosses cubital fossa, passes between pronator teres heads, travels between FDS and FDP, then through carpal tunnel.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Most forearm flexors/pronators via median and anterior interosseous nerves; thenar muscles via recurrent branch; first two lumbricals.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Lateral palm and palmar lateral 3½ digits; dorsal distal phalanges/nail beds of same digits.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal lesion causes weak pronation, wrist/finger flexion and thenar function; carpal tunnel causes thenar weakness and paresthesia in lateral 3½ digits, usually sparing central palm.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior interosseus nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Predominantly C8–T1 fibres carried in median nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Branches from median nerve in proximal forearm and descends on anterior interosseous membrane with anterior interosseous artery.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Flexor pollicis longus, lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus and pronator quadratus.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: No cutaneous territory; articular/proprioceptive fibres to wrist and distal radioulnar joints.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes weakness of thumb IP and index DIP flexion, producing an abnormal pinch/OK sign without cutaneous sensory loss.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common palmar digital nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branches of median nerve in the palm.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Run distally in palm toward interdigital clefts, superficial to flexor tendons.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Some median common digital branches may carry motor fibres to first/second lumbricals before terminal sensory division.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Divide into proper palmar digital nerves supplying adjacent sides of lateral digits.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Injury produces sensory loss in adjacent digital territories and may affect associated lumbrical branch depending on level.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C8–T1, with occasional C7 contribution; terminal branch of medial cord.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends medial arm, passes posterior to medial epicondyle, enters forearm between FCU heads, travels with ulnar artery distally and enters hand through Guyon’s canal.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: FCU and medial half of FDP in forearm; most intrinsic hand muscles through deep branch.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Medial 1½ digits and adjacent hand through palmar and dorsal cutaneous/superficial branches.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Weak finger abduction/adduction and key pinch with sensory loss in ulnar digits; lesion at elbow may also weaken FCU/FDP. Froment sign may be positive.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C8–T1, with occasional C7 contribution.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: At the wrist enters the hand superficial to flexor retinaculum through Guyon’s canal, then divides into superficial and deep branches.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: At hand level, motor supply is chiefly via deep branch to hypothenar muscles, interossei, medial lumbricals, adductor pollicis and deep head of FPB.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Superficial branch supplies palmar aspects of medial 1½ digits; dorsal cutaneous branch arises proximal to the wrist.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Guyon’s canal lesion causes intrinsic hand weakness with variable palmar ulnar sensory loss while dorsal ulnar hand sensation may be spared.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C8–T1 fibres from ulnar nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Arises in distal forearm, passes dorsally around ulna to dorsomedial hand.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; cutaneous branch.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Dorsomedial hand and dorsal proximal parts of medial 1½ digits, with variable distribution.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory disturbance over dorsoulnar hand; spared in lesions confined to Guyon’s canal because branch arises proximal to wrist.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep branch of ulnar nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes deep across palm with deep branch of ulnar artery around hook of hamate and across metacarpal bases.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Hypothenar muscles, interossei, medial two lumbricals, adductor pollicis and usually deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: No significant cutaneous territory; carries articular/proprioceptive fibres.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Produces intrinsic hand weakness, impaired finger abduction/adduction and weak key pinch without major cutaneous sensory loss.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial branch of ulnar nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Continues superficially in palm after ulnar nerve divides in Guyon’s canal.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Usually supplies palmaris brevis; otherwise mainly sensory.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Palmar surface of little finger and ulnar half of ring finger via proper/common palmar digital nerves.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Produces sensory loss in palmar medial 1½ digits with relatively preserved deep intrinsic motor function if deep branch is spared.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common palmar digital nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Ulnar common palmar digital branch from superficial branch of ulnar nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs distally toward the fourth interdigital cleft and divides into proper digital nerves.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None of major intrinsic muscles; mainly sensory.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of ring and little fingers on palmar aspect.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Produces sensory disturbance in its digital territory.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radial nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C5–T1 from posterior cord.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves axilla through triangular interval with profunda brachii, winds in radial groove, pierces lateral intermuscular septum, then divides near lateral elbow into superficial and deep branches.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis, ECRL and via deep/posterior interosseous branch most forearm extensors.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Posterior arm and forearm, lower lateral arm, and dorsolateral hand through cutaneous branches and superficial radial nerve.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Deficit depends on level; radial groove lesion classically causes wrist/finger extension weakness and dorsal hand sensory loss while triceps is largely spared.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial branch of the radial nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: C6–C8 fibres from radial nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends under brachioradialis with radial artery, becomes superficial in distal forearm and crosses to dorsolateral hand.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory terminal branch.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Dorsolateral hand and proximal dorsal surfaces of lateral digits, usually excluding fingertips/nail beds.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Produces numbness or neuropathic pain over dorsolateral hand without motor weakness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Scapula

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Humeral head at glenoid cavity and clavicle at acromioclavicular joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Spine, acromion, coracoid process, glenoid cavity, supraglenoid/infraglenoid tubercles, supra- and infraspinous fossae, subscapular fossa, borders and angles.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Rotator cuff muscles, deltoid, trapezius, biceps/triceps long heads, coracobrachialis, pectoralis minor, rhomboids, levator scapulae, serratus anterior and teres muscles.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Glenoid faces laterally; spine and infraspinous fossa posteriorly; subscapular fossa anteriorly; inferior angle points down.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Spine of the scapula

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Posterior scapula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Trapezius attaches superiorly and deltoid inferiorly; both continue onto acromion.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Separates supraspinous and infraspinous fossae and expands laterally into acromion.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Palpable posterior landmark used to orient the scapula and identify the approximate T3 vertebral level medially.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coracoid process

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Scapula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Short head of biceps and coracobrachialis arise from tip; pectoralis minor inserts medially; coracoacromial, coracoclavicular and coracohumeral ligaments attach.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Projects anterolaterally superior to glenoid; palpable below lateral clavicle.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important surgical and surface landmark; involved in coracoclavicular stabilisation of AC joint.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Clavicle

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Manubrium medially at sternoclavicular joint and acromion laterally at acromioclavicular joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Sternal end, acromial end, conoid tubercle, trapezoid line, subclavian groove and impression for costoclavicular ligament.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Pectoralis major, deltoid, trapezius, sternocleidomastoid and subclavius.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Bulky sternal end medial; flattened acromial end lateral; medial two-thirds convex anteriorly and lateral third concave anteriorly; conoid tubercle inferior/posterior.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Humerus

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Scapula proximally at glenohumeral joint; radius and ulna distally at elbow.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, anatomical/surgical necks, greater/lesser tubercles, intertubercular sulcus, deltoid tuberosity, radial groove, capitulum, trochlea, epicondyles and fossae.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Rotator cuff on tubercles; pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi and teres major around intertubercular sulcus; deltoid on tuberosity; forearm flexor/extensor groups arise from epicondyles.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Head faces medially, superiorly and slightly posteriorly; olecranon fossa is posterior; capitulum is lateral and trochlea medial.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial epicondyle of the humerus

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal humerus.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Common flexor-pronator tendon and ulnar collateral ligament.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve passes posterior to it in the cubital tunnel region.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Ulnar nerve is vulnerable here; common site of traction injury/medial epicondylitis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal humerus.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Common extensor tendon, supinator and radial collateral/lateral ulnar collateral ligament complex.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies lateral to capitulum; radial nerve divides anterior to lateral elbow region.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Common extensor origin is involved in lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow).

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Olecranon

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Proximal ulna.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Triceps inserts posteriorly/superiorly; flexor carpi ulnaris arises partly from it; elbow capsule and collateral structures attach around it.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms posterior point of elbow and enters olecranon fossa during extension.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Subcutaneous bursa over it can inflame (olecranon bursitis); fractures may disrupt triceps mechanism.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulna

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Trochlea of humerus, radial head proximally, radius distally; does not directly articulate with carpal bones.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Olecranon, coronoid process, trochlear notch, radial notch, ulnar tuberosity, shaft, head and styloid process.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Triceps, brachialis, FCU, FDP, pronator quadratus, supinator and multiple deep forearm muscles.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Trochlear notch faces anteriorly; radial notch is lateral; olecranon posterior/superior; styloid lies distally and medially/posteriorly.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radius

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Capitulum of humerus and ulna proximally; ulna and scaphoid/lunate distally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, neck, radial tuberosity, shaft, ulnar notch, dorsal tubercle and styloid process.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Biceps inserts on radial tuberosity; pronator teres and pronator quadratus insert on radius; supinator inserts proximally; multiple thumb muscles arise from shaft.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Disc-shaped head proximal; tuberosity faces medially; styloid distal/lateral; dorsal tubercle posterior.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pisiform

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with triquetrum on its dorsal surface.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Small pea-shaped sesamoid carpal bone in flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Flexor carpi ulnaris inserts; abductor digiti minimi arises; pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments continue force distally.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Located on palmar/ulnar aspect of proximal carpus; articular facet faces dorsally.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Forms medial boundary of Guyon’s canal and is a palpable landmark at ulnar wrist.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Carpus (carpal bones)

cards.question: Components
cards.answer: Proximal row lateral to medial: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform. Distal row: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Radius and articular disc proximally; metacarpals distally; extensive intercarpal articulations.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Scaphoid tubercle and trapezium laterally; pisiform and hook of hamate medially form bony margins of carpal tunnel.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the wrist skeleton, permitting mobility while transmitting load from hand to forearm.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Scaphoid/trapezium lie radial; pisiform/hamate ulnar; concave palmar carpal arch is bridged by flexor retinaculum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: 2nd metacarpal bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Trapezoid mainly, with trapezium/capitate and adjacent metacarpal bases variably; proximal phalanx of index finger distally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Base, shaft and head.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis longus insert at base; dorsal and palmar interossei arise from shaft surfaces.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Base proximal, rounded head distal; radial side belongs toward thumb; shaft lies between first and third metacarpals.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Proximal phalanx (I), middle phalanx (II), distal phalanx (III)

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Proximal phalanx with metacarpal and middle phalanx; middle with proximal/distal phalanges; distal with middle phalanx.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Each has base, shaft and head except distal phalanx, which has a terminal tuft.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on middle phalanx; flexor digitorum profundus on distal phalanx; extensor expansion attaches across middle/distal phalanges; intrinsic hand muscles attach to proximal phalanges/extensor expansions.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Bases are proximal and heads distal; distal phalanges have broad terminal tufts; palmar surfaces relate to flexor sheaths.
